title: Vanishing of shriek sections near a disjoint closed subset
statement: Let $j:U\to X$ be a weakly etale morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-weakly-etale-morphism] and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with $U\times_X Z=\varnothing$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $V\to X$ be an affine object of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-small-proetale-site] such that every point of $V$ specializes to a point of $V_Z=V\times_X Z$. For every abelian sheaf $G$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] on $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$, $(j_!G)(V)=0$, where $j_!G$ is the abelian sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of the presheaf $W\mapsto\bigoplus_{\varphi:W\to U\text{ over }X}G(W\xrightarrow{\varphi}U)$ [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf, lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization].

proof.text: Write $P$ for the displayed direct-sum presheaf. The local-sections theorem applies first to its underlying set presheaf. Its set sheafification acquires addition by choosing local representatives for two sections on a common refinement and adding them in $P$; local equality of representatives makes this independent of choices. Negation sends a local representative $p$ to $-p$; local equality makes it well-defined. Zero is the image of $0\in P(W)$ on each object $W$. Restricting any of these representatives gives the representative of the restricted operation, so these operations define an abelian presheaf structure. The group identities hold on local representatives and therefore hold globally by sheaf uniqueness. Any map of abelian presheaves from $P$ to an abelian sheaf factors through the set sheafification and respects these operations locally, hence globally. By the universal property this is the abelian sheafification $j_!G$. Thus every section of $j_!G$ is locally the image of a section of $P$.

Fix $s\in(j_!G)(V)$ and choose a covering on which it is represented in $P$ as in step 1. The covering definition, applied to the affine $V$, refines it to finitely many affine arrows $T_a\to V$ whose images cover $V$. Pull back the representatives to these affines. By stability of closed immersions under base change, $C_a=Z\times_XT_a\to T_a$ is a closed immersion; write $T_a=\operatorname{Spec}A_a$ and $C_a=\operatorname{Spec}(A_a/I_a)$ using the affine description of a closed immersion. No finiteness of $I_a$ is asserted. Open immersions are weakly etale and composing with the original covering arrows remains weakly etale, as stated in the weakly etale localization lemma.

For each $a$, form $W_a=\operatorname{Spec}(S_a^{-1}A_a)$ with $S_a$ the elements invertible modulo $I_a$. The localization lemma makes $W_a\to T_a$ weakly etale, with image the points specializing to $C_a$, and makes every point of $W_a$ specialize within $W_a$ to a point over $C_a$. Composition gives an object $W_a\to V\to X$ of the pro-etale site. To see that the $W_a\to V$ cover, choose any $v\in V$ and a specialization $z\in V_Z$ of $v$. Some $t\in T_a$ lies above $z$ because the $T_a$ cover. It belongs to $C_a$. The map $T_a\to V$ is flat since it is weakly etale, so generalization lifting supplies $t\prime$ specializing to $t$ and mapping to $v$. Hence $t\prime$ is in the image of $W_a$, and $v$ is in the image of $W_a\to V$. To check the covering definition on every affine open $H\subseteq V$, use the affine-transition assertion of the spectrum-colimit lemma on the two-object directed ring diagram $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)\to\Gamma(W_a,\mathcal O_{W_a})$. It says $W_a\to V$ is affine. By the definition of an affine morphism, the inverse image $W_{a,H}$ of $H$ is an affine open of $W_a$. The finite family of these opens has images with union $H$, by the surjectivity just proved. Thus the affine-open condition holds for every $H$, and the weakly etale arrows $W_a\to V$ are a pro-etale covering.

If $W_a$ is nonempty and an $X$-morphism $W_a\to U$ existed, choose a point of $W_a$ and then its specialization lying over $C_a$. Write $q$ for that latter point and $\mathfrak q$ for its prime in $S_a^{-1}A_a$. Its contraction contains $I_a$, so the canonical map $A_a\to\kappa(q)$ annihilates $I_a$ and factors through $A_a/I_a$. Applying $\operatorname{Spec}$ gives a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(q)\to C_a\to Z$ compatible over $X$ with $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(q)\to W_a\to U$. The fiber-product universal property gives a morphism from this nonempty one-point spectrum to $U\times_XZ=\varnothing$, a contradiction. Thus the indexing set for $P(W_a)$ is empty, and $P(W_a)=0$. If $W_a=\varnothing$, it has a unique map to $U$; the empty covering and the sheaf axiom give $G(\varnothing\to U)=0$, so again $P(W_a)=0$.

The representatives of $s$ on $T_a$ restrict to elements of $P(W_a)=0$. Naturality of the sheafification map therefore gives $s|_{W_a}=0$ for all $a$. Since step 3 gives a covering, sheaf uniqueness implies $s=0$. Every section is zero, as required. If $V$ is empty, its empty cover gives the same conclusion directly.
